examples.question_text: A rectangle is $7\text{ cm}$ long and $5\text{ cm}$ wide. Its length is increased by $2\text{ cm}$ while its width stays the same. Find the new area and how much the area increases.
examples.solution_text:
Original area
$\begin{align*}A&=7\times5\\&=35\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
New length: $7+2=9\text{ cm}$.
New area
$\begin{align*}A&=9\times5\\&=45\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$45-35=10\text{ cm}^{2}$
The area increases by $10\text{ cm}^{2}$.

examples.question_text: A rectangular floor is $5.6\text{ m}$ long and $2.7\text{ m}$ wide. Rectangular tiles are $40\text{ cm}$ long and $30\text{ cm}$ wide. The tiles are placed with their lengths along the length of the floor. How many tiles are needed?
examples.solution_text:
Use centimetres for all the lengths.
$5.6\text{ m}=560\text{ cm}$ and $2.7\text{ m}=270\text{ cm}$.
Area of the floor
$\begin{align*}A&=560\times270\\&=151200\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
Area of one tile
$\begin{align*}A&=40\times30\\&=1200\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$151200\div1200=126$
$126$ tiles are needed.

examples.question_text: A rectangular wall is $8\text{ m}$ long and $4.5\text{ m}$ high. One litre of paint covers $9\text{ m}^{2}$. How many litres are needed to paint the wall?
examples.solution_text:
Area of the wall
$\begin{align*}A&=8\times4.5\\&=36\text{ m}^{2}\end{align*}$
$36\div9=4$
$4$ litres of paint are needed.

Rectangle A
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{A}}&=8\times3\\&=24\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
Square B
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{B}}&=5\times5\\&=25\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$25-24=1\text{ cm}^{2}$
Square B has the larger area, by $1\text{ cm}^{2}$.

examples.question_text: A rectangle measures $4\text{ cm}$ by $3\text{ cm}$. Both dimensions are doubled. Find the new area and state how many times as large it is as the original.
examples.solution_text:
Original area
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{original}}&=4\times3\\&=12\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
New dimensions: $8\text{ cm}$ and $6\text{ cm}$.
New area
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{new}}&=8\times6\\&=48\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
$48\div12=4$
The new area is $48\text{ cm}^{2}$, which is $4$ times the original.

examples.question_text: A rectangle measures $10\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$. Find its area. Compare the area increases when only the length increases by $2\text{ cm}$ and when only the width increases by $2\text{ cm}$. Which change gives the greater increase?
examples.solution_text:
Original area
$\begin{align*}A&=10\times6\\&=60\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
Length increased by $2\text{ cm}$
$\begin{align*}A&=12\times6\\&=72\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
Increase: $72-60=12\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Width increased by $2\text{ cm}$ instead
$\begin{align*}A&=10\times8\\&=80\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
Increase: $80-60=20\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Increasing the width, the smaller dimension, gives the greater area increase.
